thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired: incident=PD-84723 severity=high service=edge-ingress-health message=TLS handshake failures / LB target flapping in eu-west-1 :rotating_light:
pagerduty: Paging alex (oncall) -> escalation policy: infra-primary -> if unacked 90s escalate to maria (sre)
alex (oncall): Acked. Looking. What’s the initial customer impact?
maria (sre): I’m standing by. If this is TLS + target health we might be seeing certificate renewals + backend deployment overlap. Will pull the LB target group health now.
sam (netops): Seeing increased TLS handshake error rate from our edge logs: `TLSErr: alert handshake_failure` fded across 10% of connections in eu-west-1 over the last 4m. Also a small spike in 502/504 from the ALB.
nicole (prod): Reports from GAUGE: ~4.8% request failures for EU customers hitting realtime endpoints, some long tail latency. Customers reporting errors in-app via support. Maya, can you quantify tickets?
maya (support): 7 tickets so far (5x EU webapp, 2x mobile). All reference "Something went wrong" with timestamp around 12:23UTC. Adding pending customer-impact note in incident channel.
alex (oncall): Quick checks: `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:tg:eu-west-1:...` shows about 6/20 targets Unhealthy (timeout) and status reason `Health checks failed (TLS/443)`.
jordan (eng): We rolled a model-serving canary in eu-west-1 ~12:18UTC that touched the same target group. Could be related. Canary used a new nginx sidecar with TLS passthrough tweak.
maria (sre): Top hypothesis: new canary + certificate chain mismatch on the sidecar causing backend handshakes to fail -> LB sees targets as unhealthy -> edge shows handshake errors.
sam (netops): Also saw Route53 change earlier: `change-id Z3ABC... submitted 12:10UTC` with TTL=60 for a weighted-record update. Might be unrelated but noting.
alex (oncall): Mitigation plan: 1) Pause traffic to canary (remove from target group), 2) re-register healthy instances if needed, 3) clear edge-level cache, 4) if TLS cert issue, fail traffic to backup cert. I'll start with (1).
alex (oncall): `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:tg:... --targets Id=i-0abcd1234` removing canary nodes now.
(30s later) alex (oncall): Deregister complete. Observing target count down to 14 healthy / 20 -> giving time for health checks to re-evaluate.
devops-bot: Deploy bot: rollback request submitted by alex — canary deployment halted.
maria (sre): Good. Re-check ALB metrics: healthy targets rising to 17/20, TLS handshake errors dropping in edge logs from 10% -> 3% in 2 min. Keep monitoring for 10 min before full close.
jordan (eng): I’ll open a PR to revert the sidecar TLS config and add a stricter integration test around cert chain validation to prevent future flips.
nicole (prod): Customer comms draft: "We're investigating a regional edge degradation affecting EU users, mitigations in progress. We'll update in 30m." Maya will own initial outreach.
maya (support): Draft posted to #customer-incidents, tagging affected customers.
sam (netops): Quick DNS check: `dig +short edge.redwood-inference.com @8.8.8.8` still returns eu-west-1 weighted records; change pending from 12:10UTC shows still INSYNC. No propagation issues observed.
alex (oncall): Extra check for certs: `openssl s_client -connect internal:443 -servername svc.example` returns `verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate` on one canary host. This aligns with chain mismatch.
maria (sre): Given improvement, action items: - jordan revert sidecar (in progress) - add integration test - roll certs if we see more chain errors - set canary traffic ramp to 0 for 24h until tests added.
alex (oncall): Escalation rule: if healthy targets < 12 or errors > 7% for 5m -> auto-escalate to infra-lead. Current metrics: healthy 17/20, errors 2.9% (5m avg). Good for now.
pagerduty: Escalation timer reset after ack by alex.
jordan (eng): PR opened: #8942 revert sidecar config + test. Will request review from sam.
maria (sre): Recommend increase health-check timeout to reduce flapping during graceful shutdowns — I’ll run a small config change in a canary TG.
sam (netops): Agreed. I'll coordinate with alex on staggered re-register to avoid thundering herd.
nicole (prod): ETA for customer update? If metrics stable in 10m we can send "issue mitigated, root cause under investigation".
maya (support): Sending interim update now.
(6m later) alex (oncall): 10m monitor window complete. Metrics stable. No new tickets in last 6m.
maria (sre): Closing the active pager for now. Will convert to follow-up action item doc: investigation/PR tracebacks, cert chain root cause, improved canary test, and a runbook tweak to pause canary on TLS errors.
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-84723 acknowledged by alex (oncall) and closed (status=resolved) at 2967212410.
nicole (prod): Thanks team. Follow-ups: retrospective tomorrow 09:30UTC to cover process changes and customer messaging cadence.
alex (oncall): Filed post-incident ticket: INF-1027 (cause: sidecar TLS chain mismatch during canary) assigned to jordan.
jordan (eng): On it, will add test and coordinate rollout plan.
maya (support): Noted — will follow up with customers who logged tickets once RCA ready.
(added :white_check_mark: reactions by maria (sre) and sam (netops))
